Discussed integration models (marketplace listing, Dedicated on Apex infra, Private/VPC options), technical compatibility (GPUs, kernels, quantization), security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and next steps to run benchmarks and schedule a SE-led technical deep dive.

Technical compatibility: GPUs (A100/H100), kernel/quantization support, KV cache and batching

transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-04-30 16:00 PDT - Duration 53m
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ethan Liu (Redwood Partnerships); Liam O'Neill, Sarah Chen, Marcus Wu, Anita Gomez (ApexCloud)

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jamie Ortega from Redwood, really excited to kick this off. Quick intros?
[00:12] Liam: Yeah hi I'm Liam, head of partnerships at ApexCloud, thanks for setting this up. Sarah's on the call to talk ops and marketplace, Marcus will cover technical & architecture, Anita will handle security.
[00:25] Jamie: Great. Priya, Ethan?
[00:28] Priya: Hey all, Priya Shah, SE at Redwood, I'll own the technical deep dive and benchmarks.
[00:33] Ethan: Ethan Liu, partnerships, happy to coordinate go-to-market.
[00:38] [00:40] Liam: For context, ApexCloud offers managed GPU clusters across NA/EU, we have a marketplace team and we're exploring partner integrations for inference stacks, we saw Redwood's runtime and the performance stories looked interesting.
[00:55] Jamie: Awesome. High level, we typically partner two ways: 1) list Redwood as a marketplace integration (hosted API endpoints or marketplace-managed billing) or 2) deploy Redwood Dedicated on partner infra so customers can buy reserved capacity directly on Apex. There's also private deployments for regulated customers.
[01:20] Sarah: Marketplace listing is attractive - we want to understand what artifacts you need and what the certification bar is. Also curious about billing/quoting flow.
[01:33] Jamie: We have a checklist - docs, performance profiles, support SLA. For billing we can integrate with marketplace metering but we'll need to map token units and embed pricing. I'll send the deck.
[01:46] Marcus: On the technical side, what hardware does Redwood support? We run A100 and H100 clusters, NVLink fabrics, mixed instance families. Any kernel compatibility notes?
[01:58] Priya: We support A100/H100, and we've optimised kernels across Ampere and Hopper. There is some nuance with H100 kernel selection for certain quantized paths; we'll want to validate CUDA/nvcc versions, NCCL and the driver matrix. Also if you're running multi-tenant clusters we need to discuss isolation for KV cache and prefix caching.
[02:25] Marcus: KV cache? We saw notes about KV -> we sometimes see it called K-V cash in older docs - can you clarify behaviour for long-context workloads?
[02:35] Priya: Sure - KV cache is our name for the key/value attention cache that we keep in-GPU memory for serving long contexts; it matters for memory sizing and how we shard across GPUs. For very long-history workloads the cache can be pinned to a subset of nodes; more on that in a deep dive.
[02:54] [03:00] Anita: Security questions up front: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS integration, and audit logs. Do you provide a private control plane for customers?
[03:12] Jamie: Yes, we offer a Private deployment option with a customer-managed control plane, and integrations with KMS/HSM for key management. We also publish SOC 2 artifacts and a security whitepaper - will share.
[03:26] Anita: For private deployments, what about network topology? VPC peering, no inbound except through a VPN?
[03:33] Priya: We support VPC peering, customer-managed networking, and can run in an air-gapped mode in on-prem installs. There are deployment patterns depending on latency and data residency needs.
[03:46] [04:00] Liam: From a product POV, our marketplace needs an operations runbook and health checks so we can automate listing status. We also want to define co-selling playbooks - are you open to joint-engineered templates?
[04:12] Ethan: Absolutely - we typically co-author a partner pack and can do co-marketing. We can provide joint benchmarks and customer references as we go.
[04:23] Sarah: Benchmarks - what metrics should we run? p50/p95 latency, throughput at concurrency X, token cost?
[04:30] Priya: Yes p50/p95, throughput, and token-per-second cost are objective metrics. We'll share a spreadsheet where you can drop in your workload profile; Marcus please send sample prompts and expected max length.
[04:45] Marcus: We'll do that. Also curious about quantization: do you recommend int8 or 4-bit for cost-sensitive workloads? Any quality regressions you've seen?
[04:56] Priya: We provide quantization profiles - int8/4-bit paths generally reduce memory and increase throughput but some model families have regen issues at 4-bit; our Optimize team has recommendations per model. We'll include suggested fallback policies in the doc.
[05:15] [05:30] Liam: On business model - what does partner margin look like for marketplace or dedicated sales? Do you do referral fees, revenue share, or reseller agreements?
[05:40] Jamie: We have multiple options: marketplace listing with referral fees, co-sell revenue split on dedicated capacity, and enterprise reseller agreements for Private deployments. We can tailor contracts depending on commitment levels.
[05:52] Sarah: Legal/Procurement will need a sample MOU and SLA.
[05:58] Jamie: We'll draft an MOU and share standard SLA templates.
[06:04] [06:20] Marcus: A couple of deep dive items - 1) kernel/drivers and NCCL versions, 2) memory/kv-sharding patterns, 3) scheduling for continuous batching, 4) observability hooks (traces, per-route latency, per-token billing).
[06:36] Priya: We'll cover all those in the technical session. For observability we expose per-route metrics, token counts, and tracing hooks that can pull into your console. There are also options to emit audit logs to customer S3 for Private installs.
[06:55] [07:10] Anita: Encryption at rest for model weights? If deployed on Apex infra who holds the keys?
[07:18] Priya: For Private deployments the customer can own the keys via KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we can integrate with partner KMS so keys can be managed by you or by the customer, depending on the architecture.
[07:31] [07:45] Liam: Thinking of timelines - if we wanted to run a joint pilot with a few existing customers, what's a reasonable ramp? 6-8 weeks?
[07:55] Jamie: Pilot timeline depends on integrations: a marketplace listing + hosted demo can be quick (2-4 weeks), Dedicated pilot with reserved infra and benchmarks usually 6-10 weeks. We'll scope once we see workload profile.
[08:12] [08:30] Marcus: Network and latency - what p95s can we expect for typical prompt lengths? Example: 1k tokens with batch concurrency of 8.
[08:40] Priya: Ballpark: for a 7B-ish model on A100 optimized path, p50 ~50-80ms per request; p95 depends on batching and prefix cache hit rate. We'll run targeted benchmarks so we don't throw out inaccurate numbers. (note: transcription sometimes swaps units - we'll validate in the spreadsheet)
[09:05] [09:20] Sarah: Ok. A few ecosystem questions: do you support function/tool-calling and streaming, and how do you bill for streaming tokens?
[09:31] Jamie: We support streaming and tool calls; billing is token-based including stream tokens - we'll include how we meter streaming sessions.
[09:40] Ethan: One more angle: marketplace onboarding - we need sample integration points for provisioning, metering hooks, and support SLAs.
[09:49] Jamie: We'll provide a checklist and API examples for provisioning and metering.
[10:00] [10:15] Liam: Any concerns on your side about running on partner-managed infra? Multi-tenancy isolation, noisy neighbor?
[10:25] Priya: Noisy neighbor is real; we recommend reserved pools for partners selling dedicated capacity and kernel-level QoS; for multi-tenant hosted we do per-tenant quotas and autoscale pools. We'll share best practices.
[10:40] [11:00] Marcus: For private on-prem installs what's the upgrade path for model versions and rollouts?
[11:10] Priya: We support canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. Private deployments can be configured to pull updates from a vetted channel; we also support air-gapped upgrades via bundle.
[11:26] [11:45] Anita: Data residency - some of our customers in EU require logs never leave region. Can you constrain telemetry and logs regionally?
[11:56] Jamie: Yes, with Private or Dedicated you can pin region and retention for logs; hosted API has regional options but we'll need to discuss specifics per account.
[12:10] [12:30] Marcus: Let's talk about a quick benchmark plan: Marcus to send workloads; Redwood SE will run runs on a comparable Apex node or provide a lab result; compare p95 and token cost across quantization profiles.
[12:45] Priya: We'll need SSH or access details for test infra if you want us to run on Apex nodes; otherwise we can run equivalent configs on Redwood testbeds and you can run a follow-up on your infra.
[13:00] Sarah: Operationally, support handoff - who owns triage for customer incidents on dedicated infra?
[13:12] Jamie: For Dedicated, joint ops model: Redwood handles runtime bugs and model-serving issues; partner handles infra/hypervisor issues. We define runbooks.
[13:25] [13:40] Ethan: OK let's recap and next steps.
[13:45] Jamie: Recap: 1) Redwood to share partner deck, security whitepaper, and benchmark spreadsheet. 2) Marcus to send workload sample & infra details. 3) Schedule SE deep dive week of 2026-05-04. 4) Legal to start MOU draft.
[14:05] Liam: Sounds good. Any last quick Qs?
[14:10] Anita: One more: compliance evidence for SOC2 - can you share a summary and attestations?
[14:15] Jamie: Yes will share SOC2 summary and we can set up a security review if needed.
[14:22] Sarah: Thanks all.
[14:25] Jamie: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links and action items.
[14:30] [End of recording - note: actual call continued through detailed logistics offline; transcript truncated to main discussion points. Some transcriptions contain minor errors (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "coast" instead of cost in a few places).]
